text:
The quantum Fisher (Fubini‑Study) metric for a pure state written in Madelung form is  

\[
g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}
 = \frac{1}{\hbar^{2}}\operatorname{Cov}\!\bigl(\partial_\mu S,\partial_\nu S\bigr)
   +\frac{1}{4}\,\mathbb{E}\!\bigl[\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal P\,\partial_\nu\ln\mathcal P\bigr].
\]

Using the definitions  

\[
\pi_\mu = \frac{1}{m}\,\partial_\mu S ,\qquad 
u_\mu   = \frac{\hbar}{2m}\,\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal P ,
\]

we have  

\[
\operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu,\pi_\nu)=\frac{1}{m^{2}}\operatorname{Cov}(\partial_\mu S,\partial_\nu S),\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu,u_\nu)=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{4m^{2}}\,
\mathbb{E}\bigl[\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal P\,\partial_\nu\ln\mathcal P\bigr].
\]

Substituting these into the metric expression yields  

\[
g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}
 = \frac{m^{2}}{\hbar^{2}}\Bigl[
      \operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu,\pi_\nu)
    + \operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu,u_\nu)
   \Bigr]_{\mathcal P}.
\]

Hence the proportionality factor is  

\[
C = \frac{m^{2}}{\hbar^{2}}.
\]

Following the request to write the answer using \(x = \hbar\) and not the symbol \(\hbar\), we obtain  

\[
\boxed{C = \dfrac{m^{2}}{x^{2}}}.
\]

Thus Solution 1 provides the correct final answer.

CHOICE: 1
